title: SNAP receipt transitions do not map cleanly onto following-month material security
source_unit: SIPP identified person, adjacent reference-month pair

observations.method: Weighted descriptive comparison from the 2025 SIPP public-use file using month-t SNAP state and month-t+1 hardship; 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: Fay-BRR standard errors and 95% intervals are retained for both hardship measures; transition selection and field reference periods remain sources of non-sampling uncertainty.
observations.subgroup: SNAP nonreceipt at both adjacent months.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable nonreceipt is a reference state, not proof of security or a counterfactual for receipt transitions.

observations.method: Weighted descriptive comparison from the 2025 SIPP public-use file using month-t SNAP state and month-t+1 hardship; 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: Fay-BRR standard errors and 95% intervals are retained; the entry transition is rare and selected, and the hardship fields have their own universes and reference periods.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher following-month hardship is consistent with entry amid need, not evidence that SNAP caused hardship.

observations.method: Weighted descriptive comparison from the 2025 SIPP public-use file using month-t SNAP state and month-t+1 hardship; 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: Fay-BRR standard errors and 95% intervals are retained; the exit transition is rare and selected, and the hardship fields have their own universes and reference periods.
observations.counterinterpretation: Exit remains compatible with following hardship; it cannot be read as restored security without observing notice, reason, amount, remedy, and later outcomes.

observations.method: Weighted descriptive comparison from the 2025 SIPP public-use file using month-t SNAP state and month-t+1 hardship; 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: Fay-BRR standard errors and 95% intervals are retained; receipt persistence is selected and hardship fields have their own universes and reference periods.
observations.subgroup: SNAP receipt at both adjacent months.
observations.counterinterpretation: Continued receipt can coexist with rent, mortgage, or utility hardship; receipt and material protection are separate stages.

boundary: This is a Fay-BRR weighted descriptive SIPP transition comparison, not a SNAP program-effect estimate, complete household benefit spell, notice/effort/remedy record, or measure of trust, political meaning, or later recovery. The retrieval hash covers the committed analysis memo.
